judgments.yea_description: Voted for Legislative Bill 319, which would have restored food assistance to people with old drug convictions. Federal law bars anyone convicted of a drug felony from food assistance for life. That covers possessing, using or selling drugs. The same federal law lets a state opt out of the bar. The bill would have had Nebraska opt out. A person with such a conviction would have stayed eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program once they had finished their sentence. They would also have stayed eligible while on parole, probation or post-release supervision. The Nebraska Legislature passed it 32-17, the Governor vetoed it, and the vote to override the veto failed 24 to 24, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Legislative Bill 929, which would have kept Medicaid patients from being charged copays. The state could not have charged a Medicaid recipient a deductible, a copay, coinsurance or any similar charge, unless federal law required it. Federal law does require a charge in some cases. There, the bill would have stopped the state bringing it in before October 1, 2028. After that the charge would have had to be as light as possible. It would have been set at the federal minimum. Managed care companies would have been allowed to pay it for the patient. And a provider could not have refused care to anyone who did not pay it. The Nebraska Legislature passed it 31-18, the Governor vetoed it, and the vote to override the veto failed 22 to 26, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Legislative Bill 1029, which would have narrowed what public colleges must report about money from hostile foreign governments. Nebraska law makes a public college report funding and contracts it gets from a foreign adversarial source. The bill would have counted a contract only where it benefits that foreign source. It would also have taken salary, wages and other pay out of what has to be reported at all. Less of the money coming from those sources would have been disclosed. The Nebraska Legislature passed it 29-20, the Governor vetoed it, the Legislature did not vote to override, and it did not become law.
